title: QuickFlow: An Efficient Local Search Method to Map Convolutions on Spatial Architectures
problem: Mapping convolutions to spatial architectures requires exploring a vast mapping space with significant performance variations. Existing tools suffer from long execution times due to complex interactions between mapping decisions.
motivation: Fast, high-quality mappings are essential for enabling runtime resource allocation and hardware design space exploration in spatial architectures.
method: QuickFlow builds equivalences between mappings based on data reuse analysis and redesigns optimization around these equivalences. It performs greedy local search after quickly selecting best dataflow up to equivalence, and integrates an improved analytical model with exact tile-size formulas for arbitrary convolutions.
key_novelty: Equivalence-based mapping optimization reducing search space through dataflow equivalence analysis.
contributions: Equivalence-based optimization framework reducing mapping space exploration
Improved analytical model with exact tile-size formulas for convolutions
1-2.1× better energy-delay product compared to state-of-the-art tools
Up to 182× faster execution than best competing mapping tools
limitations: Evaluation limited to convolutional kernels; applicability to other operation types not discussed.
primary_theme: Efficient dataflow-aware mapping for spatial accelerators
